subject: maths
title: Word Problems and Number Sentences
seo_title: Year 2 Word Problems and Number Sentences Worksheets (Australian Curriculum)
standard_text: Use mathematical modelling to solve practical additive and multiplicative problems, including money transactions, representing the situation and choosing calculation strategies; interpret and communicate solutions in terms of the situation
meta_desc: Free Year 2 maths worksheets on word problems and number sentences: choose the number sentence, join and take-away stories, compare problems, missing parts, equal groups, money and two-step problems. 100 questions with pictures and an answer key, matched to the Australian Curriculum.
key_big: Picture the story. Then choose: add or subtract?
key_sub: Things join: add. Some go away, or you compare: subtract. Equal groups: add the same number again. Write a number sentence with a ? for the number you need to find.
body_html:
Picture the story first

Read the story. Ask: what is happening? Do things join, go away, or do we compare two amounts? Then write a number sentence. Use a ? for the number you do not know.

What happensStoryNumber sentence
Join (more come)26 students are on the bus. 17 more get on.26 + 17 = ?
Take away (some go)45 birds are in a tree. 18 fly away.45 − 18 = ?
CompareMia has 52 shells. Leo has 37. How many more does Mia have?52 − 37 = ?
Missing part40 students were on the bus. Some got off. 25 are left.40 − ? = 25
Equal groups3 bags with 5 apples in each bag5 + 5 + 5 = ?

Draw a bar model

A bar model shows the parts and the whole. If you know both parts, add. If you know the whole and one part, subtract.

Example

There were 40 students on the bus. Some got off. Now there are 25. How many got off?

The whole is 40 and one part is 25. Subtract: 40 − 25 = 15. Check: 40 − 15 = 25.

Answer: 15 students

Compare: how many more?

To compare, draw two bars. The extra part is the difference. Find it by subtracting.

Example

Mia has 52 shells. Leo has 37 shells. How many more shells does Mia have?

“How many more” asks for the difference, so subtract: 52 − 37 = 15. Check: 37 + 15 = 52.

Answer: 15 shells

Equal groups and two steps

When every group has the same number, add that number again and again.

Some stories have two steps. Work out the first step, then use that answer.

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Adding when the question asks “how many more”“How many more” is a difference. Subtract: 52 − 37 = 15
Using the wrong operation because of one wordPicture the story. Did things join, go away, or are you comparing?
Adding the whole and a part (40 + 25)If you know the whole, subtract to find the other part
Adding the number of groups and the number in each group (3 + 5)3 bags of 5 is 5 + 5 + 5 = 15
Stopping after step 1Read the question again. What does it ask?

faq.q: What word problems do Year 2 students solve in maths?
faq.a: In the Australian Curriculum, Year 2 students solve join, take-away, compare and missing-part problems, simple money problems and equal-group stories, and they write a number sentence to show what is happening.

faq.q: What is a number sentence in Year 2 maths?
faq.a: A number sentence uses numbers and symbols to show a story, such as 26 + 17 = ? or 40 − ? = 25. The ? stands for the number you need to find.

faq.q: How can I help my child decide whether to add or subtract?
faq.a: Ask them to picture or act out the story first. If things join, add; if some go away or you compare two amounts, subtract. Drawing a bar model helps.

faq.q: Why do children add when the question says “how many more”?
faq.a: They see the word “more” and add. “How many more” asks for the difference between two amounts, so they need to subtract the smaller number from the bigger one.

items.q: There are 5 apples in a bowl. Mum puts in 3 more. How many apples are in the bowl now? Which number sentence matches?
items.e: More are added, so add: 5 + 3 = ?. 5 + 3 = 8. Subtracting would make the number smaller, but there are more now.

items.q: There are 12 apples in a bowl. The class eats 5 at recess. How many apples are left? Which number sentence matches?
items.e: Some are taken away, so subtract. Start with the bigger number: 12 − 5 = ?. 12 − 5 = 7. Adding would give more, but some have gone.

items.q: There are 4 balls in the sports shed. The teacher brings 5 more. How many balls are there now? Which number sentence matches?
items.e: More are added, so add: 4 + 5 = ?. 4 + 5 = 9. Subtracting would make the number smaller, but there are more now.

items.q: There are 13 balls in the sports shed. Students take 8 out to play. How many balls are left in the shed? Which number sentence matches?
items.e: Some are taken away, so subtract. Start with the bigger number: 13 − 8 = ?. 13 − 8 = 5. Adding would give more, but some have gone.

items.q: There are 7 apples in a bowl and 3 apples in a bag. How many apples are there in all? Which number sentence matches?
items.e: Two groups are put together, so add: 7 + 3 = ?. 7 + 3 = 10. “In all” and “altogether” mean add.
More are added, so add: 5 + 4 = ?. 5 + 4 = 9. Subtracting would make the number smaller, but there are more now.
Some are taken away, so subtract. Start with the bigger number: 12 − 4 = ?. 12 − 4 = 8. Adding would give more, but some have gone.

items.q: 9 students are on the bus. 5 students get off. How many students are still on the bus? Which number sentence matches?
items.e: Some are taken away, so subtract. Start with the bigger number: 9 − 5 = ?. 9 − 5 = 4. Adding would give more, but some have gone.

items.e: You know the whole (11) and one part (4). Take the part away: 11 − 4 = ?. 11 − 4 = 7. Do not add the two numbers: 11 is already the total.

items.q: Ruby had 53 footy cards. She got 43 more footy cards. How many footy cards does Ruby have now?
items.e: More came, so add: 53 + 43 = 96. Answer: 96 footy cards.

items.q: Charlotte had 78 stickers. She gave 15 stickers to a friend. How many stickers does Charlotte have now?
items.e: Some went away, so subtract: 78 − 15 = 63. Answer: 63 stickers.

items.q: Lachlan has 45c. He finds 30c more. How much money does he have now?
items.e: Lachlan gets more money, so add: 45c + 30c = 75c. 4 tens + 3 tens = 7 tens, and 5 more.

items.q: There were 65 cars in the school car park. Then 13 more cars came in. How many cars are in the car park now?
items.e: More came, so add: 65 + 13 = 78. Answer: 78 cars.

items.q: The cake stall had 77 cupcakes. People bought 52 cupcakes. How many cupcakes are there now?

items.q: There were 43 students on the bus. At the next stop, 26 students got off. How many students are on the bus now?
items.e: Some went away, so subtract: 43 − 26 = 17. You cannot take 6 from 3 ones, so trade 1 ten for 10 ones first. Answer: 17 students.

items.q: There were 31 kangaroos in a paddock. 23 kangaroos hopped away. How many kangaroos are in the paddock now?
items.e: Some went away, so subtract: 31 − 23 = 8. You cannot take 3 from 1 one, so trade 1 ten for 10 ones first. Answer: 8 kangaroos.

items.q: The canteen had 68 sausage rolls. At recess, students bought 9 sausage rolls. How many sausage rolls are there now?
items.e: Some went away, so subtract: 68 − 9 = 59. You cannot take 9 from 8 ones, so trade 1 ten for 10 ones first. Answer: 59 sausage rolls.

items.q: Matilda put 29 beads on a string. Then she added 56 more beads. How many beads are on the string now?
items.e: More came, so add: 29 + 56 = 85. 9 + 6 = 15 ones. Trade 10 ones for 1 ten. Answer: 85 beads.

items.q: There were 17 birds in a gum tree. 28 more birds flew in. How many birds are in the tree now?
items.e: More came, so add: 17 + 28 = 45. 7 + 8 = 15 ones. Trade 10 ones for 1 ten. Answer: 45 birds.

items.q: Aarav has 90c. He buys a pencil for 35c. How much money does he have left?
items.e: Spending money takes it away, so subtract: 90c − 35c. 90 − 30 = 60, then 60 − 5 = 55c.

items.q: There were 37 ducks on the pond. 29 ducks swam away. How many ducks are on the pond now?
items.e: Some went away, so subtract: 37 − 29 = 8. You cannot take 9 from 7 ones, so trade 1 ten for 10 ones first. Answer: 8 ducks.

items.q: Oliver had 13 shells. At the beach, he found 47 more shells. How many shells does Oliver have now?
items.e: More came, so add: 13 + 47 = 60. 3 + 7 = 10 ones. Trade 10 ones for 1 ten. Answer: 60 shells.

items.q: The library trolley had 55 books. Mei took 46 books off it. How many books are on the trolley now?
items.e: Some went away, so subtract: 55 − 46 = 9. You cannot take 6 from 5 ones, so trade 1 ten for 10 ones first. Answer: 9 books.

items.q: There were 30 children in the pool. 14 children got out. How many children are in the pool now?
items.e: Some went away, so subtract: 30 − 14 = 16. You cannot take 4 from 0 ones, so trade 1 ten for 10 ones first. Answer: 16 children.

items.q: A tub had 18 pencils. The teacher put in 17 more pencils. How many pencils are in the tub now?
items.e: More came, so add: 18 + 17 = 35. 8 + 7 = 15 ones. Trade 10 ones for 1 ten. Answer: 35 pencils.

items.q: There were 25 ducks on the pond. 19 more ducks swam over. How many ducks are on the pond now?
items.e: More came, so add: 25 + 19 = 44. 5 + 9 = 14 ones. Trade 10 ones for 1 ten. Answer: 44 ducks.

items.q: A tub had 37 pencils. Students took 8 pencils out. How many pencils are in the tub now?
items.e: Some went away, so subtract: 37 − 8 = 29. You cannot take 8 from 7 ones, so trade 1 ten for 10 ones first. Answer: 29 pencils.

items.q: Jack has 67 beads. Chloe has 36 beads. How many more beads does Jack have than Chloe?
items.e: Find the difference. Subtract the smaller number from the bigger one: 67 − 36 = 31. Check: 36 + 31 = 67. The word “more” does not mean add here. Answer: 31 beads.

items.q: Kai read 41 pages. Liam read 14 pages. How many more pages did Kai read than Liam?

sets.title: Missing parts: some got off the bus

items.q: Oliver put 68 beads on a string. Then he took off some beads. Now there are 6 beads on the string. How many beads did Oliver take off?
items.e: Some went away. 68 − ? = 6. Count back from 68 to 6, or subtract: 68 − 6 = 62. Check: 68 − 62 = 6. Answer: 62 beads.

items.q: Mei had 55 stickers. She got some more stickers. Now she has 74 stickers. How many stickers did Mei get?
items.e: Some more came. 55 + ? = 74. Count on from 55 to 74, or subtract: 74 − 55 = 19. Check: 55 + 19 = 74. Answer: 19 stickers.

items.q: There were 90 chairs in the hall. William took some chairs out. Now there are 52 chairs in the hall. Which number sentence matches the story?
items.e: Some went away. 90 − ? = 52. Count back from 90 to 52, or subtract: 90 − 52 = 38. Check: 90 − 38 = 52. Answer: 90 − ? = 52.

items.q: A box has 63 pencils. 15 are red. The rest are blue. How many pencils are blue?
items.e: You know the whole (63) and one part (15). Take the part away: 63 − 15 = 48. Check: 15 + 48 = 63. Answer: 48 pencils.

items.q: There were 25 birds in a gum tree. Some more birds flew in. Now there are 48 birds in the tree. How many birds flew in?
items.e: Some more came. 25 + ? = 48. Count on from 25 to 48, or subtract: 48 − 25 = 23. Check: 25 + 23 = 48. Answer: 23 birds.

items.q: Some students were on the bus. At the next stop, 8 students got off. Now there are 29 students on the bus. How many students were on the bus at first?
items.e: The start is missing. ? − 8 = 29. Put back the ones that went: 29 + 8 = 37. Check: 37 − 8 = 29. Answer: 37 students.

items.q: Lachlan had 70 footy cards. He gave some footy cards to his cousin. Now he has 18 footy cards. How many footy cards did Lachlan give away?
items.e: Some went away. 70 − ? = 18. Count back from 70 to 18, or subtract: 70 − 18 = 52. Check: 70 − 52 = 18. Answer: 52 footy cards.

items.q: Some children were in the pool. 18 more children jumped in. Now there are 55 children in the pool. Which number sentence matches the story?
items.e: The start is missing. ? + 18 = 55. Take away the ones that came: 55 − 18 = 37. Check: 37 + 18 = 55. Answer: ? + 18 = 55.

items.q: Jack has 86 footy cards. 75 are AFL cards. The rest are rugby league cards. How many are rugby league cards?
items.e: You know the whole (86) and one part (75). Take the part away: 86 − 75 = 11. Check: 75 + 11 = 86. Answer: 11 cards.

items.q: There were 25 ducks on the pond. Some more ducks swam over. Now there are 41 ducks on the pond. How many ducks swam over?
items.e: Some more came. 25 + ? = 41. Count on from 25 to 41, or subtract: 41 − 25 = 16. Check: 25 + 16 = 41. Answer: 16 ducks.

items.q: The canteen had some sausage rolls. At recess, students bought 32 sausage rolls. Now there are 18 sausage rolls. How many sausage rolls were there at first?
items.e: The start is missing. ? − 32 = 18. Put back the ones that went: 18 + 32 = 50. Check: 50 − 32 = 18. Answer: 50 sausage rolls.

items.q: Some kangaroos were in a paddock. 17 more kangaroos hopped in. Now there are 46 kangaroos in the paddock. Which number sentence matches the story?
items.e: The start is missing. ? + 17 = 46. Take away the ones that came: 46 − 17 = 29. Check: 29 + 17 = 46. Answer: ? + 17 = 46.

items.q: Ruby had 75 shells. She gave some shells to her brother. Now she has 31 shells. How many shells did Ruby give away?
items.e: Some went away. 75 − ? = 31. Count back from 75 to 31, or subtract: 75 − 31 = 44. Check: 75 − 44 = 31. Answer: 44 shells.

items.q: The canteen made 90 pies and sausage rolls. 54 are pies. How many are sausage rolls?
items.e: You know the whole (90) and one part (54). Take the part away: 90 − 54 = 36. Check: 54 + 36 = 90. Answer: 36 sausage rolls.

items.q: A tub had some pencils. Students took 46 pencils out. Now there are 38 pencils in the tub. How many pencils were in the tub at first?
items.e: The start is missing. ? − 46 = 38. Put back the ones that went: 38 + 46 = 84. Check: 84 − 46 = 38. Answer: 84 pencils.

items.q: There were 31 cars in the school car park. Then some more cars came in. Now there are 50 cars in the car park. How many cars came in?
items.e: Some more came. 31 + ? = 50. Count on from 31 to 50, or subtract: 50 − 31 = 19. Check: 31 + 19 = 50. Answer: 19 cars.

items.q: Amelia had some marbles. She won 42 more marbles. Now she has 98 marbles. Which number sentence matches the story?
items.e: The start is missing. ? + 42 = 98. Take away the ones that came: 98 − 42 = 56. Check: 56 + 42 = 98. Answer: ? + 42 = 98.

items.q: There are 24 students in the class. 11 are at the library. The rest are in the classroom. How many are in the classroom?
items.e: You know the whole (24) and one part (11). Take the part away: 24 − 11 = 13. Check: 11 + 13 = 24. Answer: 13 students.

items.q: The cake stall had some cupcakes. People bought 17 cupcakes. Now there are 47 cupcakes. How many cupcakes were there at first?
items.e: The start is missing. ? − 17 = 47. Put back the ones that went: 47 + 17 = 64. Check: 64 − 17 = 47. Answer: 64 cupcakes.

items.q: The library trolley had some books. Ethan put 14 more books on it. Now the trolley has 60 books. How many books were on the trolley at first?
items.e: The start is missing. ? + 14 = 60. Take away the ones that came: 60 − 14 = 46. Check: 46 + 14 = 60. Answer: 46 books.

items.q: There are 3 bags. Each bag has 5 apples. How many apples are there?
items.e: There are 3 equal groups of 5. Add 5 again and again: 5 + 5 + 5 = 15. Do not add 3 + 5: that counts the groups, not the things. Answer: 15 apples.
There are 4 equal groups of 2. Add 2 again and again: 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 = 8. Do not add 4 + 2: that counts the groups, not the things. Answer: 8 stickers.

items.q: There are 4 shelves. Each shelf has 3 books. How many books are there?
items.e: There are 4 equal groups of 3. Add 3 again and again: 3 + 3 + 3 + 3 = 12. Do not add 4 + 3: that counts the groups, not the things. Answer: 12 books.

items.q: The coach has 2 bags of balls. Each bag has 10 balls. How many balls are there?
items.e: There are 2 equal groups of 10. Add 10 again and again: 10 + 10 = 20. Do not add 2 + 10: that counts the groups, not the things. Answer: 20 balls.

items.q: There are 5 tables in the classroom. 4 students sit at each table. How many students are there?
items.e: There are 5 equal groups of 4. Add 4 again and again: 4 + 4 + 4 + 4 + 4 = 20. Do not add 5 + 4: that counts the groups, not the things. Answer: 20 students.

items.q: Leo buys 3 packs of juice boxes. Each pack has 4 juice boxes. How many juice boxes does he buy?
items.e: There are 3 equal groups of 4. Add 4 again and again: 4 + 4 + 4 = 12. Do not add 3 + 4: that counts the groups, not the things. Answer: 12 juice boxes.

items.q: 12 apples are shared equally into 3 bags. How many apples go in each bag?
items.e: Share them out one at a time into 3 groups. Each group gets 4, because 4 + 4 + 4 = 12. Answer: 4 apples.

items.q: The teacher shares 10 balls equally between 2 teams. How many balls does each team get?
items.e: Share them out one at a time into 2 groups. Each group gets 5, because 5 + 5 = 10. Answer: 5 balls.

items.q: Isla had 26 stickers. She got 17 more. Then she gave 9 to her sister. How many stickers does Isla have now?
items.e: Step 1: 26 + 17 = 43. Step 2: 43 − 9 = 34. Answer: 34 stickers.

items.q: There were 40 birds in a gum tree. 12 birds flew away. Then 15 more flew away. How many birds are in the tree now?
items.e: Step 1: 40 − 12 = 28. Step 2: 28 − 15 = 13. Answer: 13 birds.

items.q: There were 34 students on the bus. At the first stop, 8 got off and 12 got on. How many students are on the bus now?
items.e: Step 1: 34 − 8 = 26. Step 2: 26 + 12 = 38. Answer: 38 students.

items.q: There were 28 children in the pool. 15 more jumped in. Then 21 got out. How many children are in the pool now?
items.e: Step 1: 28 + 15 = 43. Step 2: 43 − 21 = 22. Answer: 22 children.

items.q: The canteen made 45 sausage rolls. Then it made 30 more. Students bought 28 at recess. How many sausage rolls are left?
items.e: Step 1: 45 + 30 = 75. Step 2: 75 − 28 = 47. Answer: 47 sausage rolls.

items.q: The library had 52 books on a shelf. Students borrowed 25. Then they brought back 16. How many books are on the shelf now?
items.e: Step 1: 52 − 25 = 27. Step 2: 27 + 16 = 43. Answer: 43 books.

items.q: The cake stall had 36 cupcakes. People bought 19. Then Chloe's dad brought 24 more. How many cupcakes are there now?
items.e: Step 1: 36 − 19 = 17. Step 2: 17 + 24 = 41. Answer: 41 cupcakes.

items.q: There are 60 chairs in the hall. 24 are for parents and 17 are for students. The rest are empty. How many chairs are empty?
items.e: Step 1: 60 − 24 = 36. Step 2: 36 − 17 = 19. Answer: 19 chairs.

items.q: Jack has 3 packets of pencils. Each packet has 5 pencils. Then he buys 4 more pencils. How many pencils does he have?
items.e: Step 1: 3 groups of 5: 5 + 5 + 5 = 15. Step 2: 15 + 4 = 19. Answer: 19 pencils.

items.q: Lachlan has 23 shells. Aarav has 9 more shells than Lachlan. How many shells do they have altogether?
items.e: Step 1: Aarav has 23 + 9 = 32. Step 2: Altogether: 23 + 32 = 55. Answer: 55 shells.

items.q: Kai has 90c. He buys an apple for 30c and a juice for 45c. How much money does he have left?
items.e: Step 1: 90c − 30c = 60c. Step 2: 60c − 45c = 15c. Answer: 15c.

items.q: Liam has a 50c coin and two 20c coins. He buys a pencil for 35c. How much money is left?
items.e: Step 1: 50c + 20c + 20c = 90c. Step 2: 90c − 35c = 55c. Answer: 55c.
